name: docforge
status: DRAFT, awaiting approval (Pattern M Phase 4 gate)
purpose: Docs-as-code tool for a solo developer who builds with AI. It scaffolds a documentation structure, detects drift between code and docs, uses a sandboxed AI agent to propose documentation updates and ADRs for human review, and publishes a versioned PDF manual from the Markdown source of truth (Markdown -> Pandoc -> LaTeX -> PDF).

decisions.reader_form: CLI + local preview. The reader itself is deferred to v2 [ASSUMED default #1, #4]
decisions.latex_direction: One-way MD -> LaTeX -> PDF. Importing .tex is out of scope [ASSUMED #2]
decisions.audience: Owner first, structured so it can be open-sourced [ASSUMED #5]
decisions.code_to_model: Allowed. Code goes to the Anthropic API only. The pilot is already public [ASSUMED #7]
decisions.agent_trigger: On demand, in an OpenShell sandbox. CI runs only the non-AI `check` and `build`, and CI's drift findings tell the developer when to run the agent [ASSUMED #8, reconciled with #14. See open_items]
decisions.agent_authority: Propose only. The agent outputs a patch and a report. The host applies it to a branch, and the human opens or merges the PR. The agent never pushes and never holds a GitHub token [ASSUMED #9]
decisions.drift_strictness: Warn locally. `--strict` (used in CI) errors only for ADR-worthy categories: dependencies, data, security, deployment [ASSUMED #10]
decisions.model_failure: The agent exits with code 3 and prints a message. check and build are unaffected [ASSUMED #11]
decisions.pdf_style: Neutral A4. The footer shows version, date and short SHA. No brand assets [ASSUMED #12]
decisions.mermaid_in_pdf: mermaid-cli (headless Chromium) renders each diagram to a vector PDF figure [ASSUMED #13]
decisions.openshell_role: Sandboxes the agent (egress only to api.anthropic.com, with a credential placeholder swapped at egress) and the PDF build (no egress). It does not host the reader
decisions.model: claude-sonnet-5-5 ($2 in / $10 out per 1M tokens), adaptive thinking, effort 'medium' [USER: Sonnet tier; effort ASSUMED]
decisions.dogfood: docforge documents itself. ADR-001 is Pandoc vs Quarto [ASSUMED #19]

estimates.impact_run: about 30-60K input + 5-10K output tokens, so about $0.10-0.25
estimates.bootstrap_pilot: about 150-300K input (with caching) + 60-100K output, so about $1.50-3.00
estimates.note: These are estimates. The usage ledger records the real cost of every run, and the caps are enforced in code

enforcement: Before each API call: estimate from count_tokens and refuse if run_spend + estimate > per_run_cap
task_budget (beta task-budgets-2026-03-13) so the model paces itself inside a run
Prompt caching on the system prompt + templates
Every response.usage is appended to ~/.docforge/usage.jsonl. A run is refused if monthly spend >= monthly_cap
Also recommended: a dedicated API key in its own Console workspace, with a spend limit

components.cli: docforge (Typer). Entry point for every command
components.config: docforge.toml in the target repo: doc set, impact map, manual chapter order, budget
components.templates: Markdown templates for the 13 docs + ADR (MADR-style, per your spec), CHANGELOG (Keep a Changelog), CI workflow, LaTeX template, pandoc defaults
components.checker: Structure, sections, links, ADR format, uncertain markers, drift. Deterministic, never calls the model
components.builder: pandoc + Lua filter (mermaid -> mmdc) + LaTeX engine (tectonic) -> PDF
components.agent: Anthropic Python SDK tool-runner loop. It only reaches the repo through a path-allowlisted tool layer (the policy enforcement point)
components.applier: Runs on the host. Applies the agent's patch to a new branch after the human reviews it
components.sandbox: OpenShell policies + images for the agent and the build

flow: developer changes code -> `docforge check --base main` (local or CI) -> drift findings
developer runs `docforge agent impact --base main` -> OpenShell sandbox -> out/docforge.patch + out/report.md
developer reviews the report -> `docforge apply out/docforge.patch` -> branch docforge/impact-<sha> -> the developer opens the PR

init.behavior: Creates only files that are missing and never overwrites. Idempotent. New docs are skeletons whose sections are filled with `> uncertain — verify with developer`. Writes docforge.toml with an impact map guessed from the repo's manifests. Adds documentation/build/ to .gitignore

rules.sections: the required H2 headings per doc type are present (warn; error under --strict)
rules.links: relative links and #anchors resolve (error). External links are not checked in MVP
rules.adr: file name NNN-kebab.md, contiguous numbers, a Status line from {Proposed, Accepted, Superseded, Deprecated}, and 'Superseded' names its successor (error)
rules.uncertain: counts `uncertain — verify with developer` markers per doc (info; the budget is set in config)
rules.drift: changed files in base...HEAD are mapped through impact_map to docs. A category is triggered but none of its docs changed -> finding. ADR-worthy categories -> error under --strict, otherwise warn
rules.drift_override: a commit trailer `Docs-Impact: none — <reason>` suppresses drift for that commit's files. The reason must be non-empty

build.behavior: Chapters follow the order in documentation/manual.yaml (the 14 sections from your spec). Output: TOC, numbered sections/figures/tables, cross-references, headers/footers. Version = `git describe --tags --always --dirty`, date = commit date. A Mermaid render failure falls back to the code block with a warning (an error under --strict). No network needed once the image is built

subcommands.bootstrap: First pass over an existing repo: reads code, config, CI and manifests, then drafts every doc + ADRs for the decisions it can see
subcommands.impact: Takes base...HEAD, runs the 12-question impact check from your spec, and edits only the docs that are materially affected. Proposes a CHANGELOG entry
subcommands.adr: `agent adr "<title>"` drafts the next-numbered ADR from the diff/context and the developer's note

tools_exposed_to_model.read_file: repo root only, max 200KB per call
tools_exposed_to_model.write_doc: ONLY paths matching README.md, CHANGELOG.md, docs/**. Anything else is rejected and logged as a policy event

honesty_rules: Never state behaviour it cannot point to in a file. Mark it `uncertain — verify with developer` instead
Every section it writes ends with `<!-- sources: path[:line], ... -->`
If the code disagrees with an existing doc, raise it as a DISCREPANCY in report.md. Do not silently 'fix' it
No noise edits: a doc touched without a materially changed claim is a failure
outputs: out/report.md (impact checklist answers, discrepancies, uncertain items, cost)

apply.behavior: Runs on the host. Checks that the patch touches only allowed doc paths, creates branch docforge/<task>-<shortsha>, applies and commits the patch, and prints the `gh pr create` command. It does not push automatically

usage.behavior: Prints spend per run, per month and in total from usage.jsonl

docforge_toml.impact_map: array of { category: string, globs: string[], docs: string[], adr_worthy: bool }

manual.chapters: string[] of doc paths, in order

has: a detailed README (architecture, trust boundary, security table, verification)
adr_candidates_visible_in_code: One client-side markdown pipeline; the server never parses markdown
Sanitizer placed directly after rehype-raw (the trust boundary)
PDF via a stateless Playwright print service rendering posted HTML
Container hardening: loopback bind, read-only, cap_drop ALL
Repairs are applied to the rendering only and always reported
pilot_observations.tension: The README already holds deep architecture and security content. The bootstrap must MOVE it into docs/ and link to it (your spec says no two copies), and must propose trimming the README as a separate, clearly flagged change

agent_sandbox.filesystem: read: /sandbox/repo (a copy of the working tree); write: /sandbox/out only
agent_sandbox.network: Only api.anthropic.com:443, via the attached 'anthropic' provider. Inside the sandbox ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is a placeholder that the OpenShell proxy swaps for the real key at egress (per the CLI's `sandbox provider attach` docs). All other egress is denied

build_sandbox.image: pandoc + tectonic (with a pre-warmed package cache) + mermaid-cli + chromium
build_sandbox.note: Tectonic fetches LaTeX packages on first use. The cache must be warmed while the image is built, or the offline build fails

openshell_runtime.uncertain: The provider syntax was verified against deploy/man/openshell.1.md in NVIDIA/OpenShell main (2026-09-29). Policy field names are still to be verified with `openshell policy --help` on the installed version
provider_setup: openshell provider create --name anthropic --type anthropic --credential ANTHROPIC_API_KEY   # bare KEY form reads the env var, so the key stays out of shell history

error_behavior.api_4xx_5xx_or_timeout: SDK retries (2), then exit 3. A partial patch is discarded, never half-written
error_behavior.budget_exceeded: exit 3 before the call is made. The ledger records the refusal
error_behavior.patch_touches_non_doc_path: apply refuses with exit 1 and lists the offending paths

out_of_scope_mvp: Reader UI (`serve`). v2 PROPOSAL: reuse markdown-visualiser as the reader instead of building a new one
Running the agent inside GitHub Actions
open_items: Confirm: the agent runs on demand in OpenShell, and CI stays AI-free (resolves the tension between defaults #8 and #14)
Confirm: the v2 reader reuses markdown-visualiser
Confirm: the bootstrap PR on markdown-visualiser may propose trimming its README in favour of docs/
